summary: Singhathon Narāsabho works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He completed his PhD at Visva-Bharati University under the doctoral supervision of Sudhindra Chandra Chakravarti.

Siniruddha Dash is a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He served as Director at the University of Madras (2000–2014), the Oriental Research Institute and Manuscripts Library (attested 2013), and the K. V. Sarma Research Foundation (2020).

Siran Upendra Deraniyagala (1942–2021) was an archaeologist who studied at Trinity College, Cambridge, the University of London under Frank Raymond Allchin, and Harvard University. He served as Director General of the Department of Archaeology, Sri Lanka (~1992–2001).

Sisir Roy is a scholar in philosophy who studied under Debabrata Sensharma. He served as a professor at the Indian Statistical Institute in 1993 and was affiliated with the National Institute of Advanced Studies (attested 2009).
Sita Krishna Nambiar was an Indologist and philosopher who studied under Paul Hacker at the University of Bonn. She held an academic post at Indraprastha College for Women.

Sita Ram Roy worked in history, archaeology, and Indology, completing doctoral studies under Anant Sadashiv Altekar and Ram Sharan Sharma. He held posts at the K. P. Jayaswal Research Institute, the Gaya Museum, and the Directorate of Archaeology and Museums, Bihar.
Siu-tong Kwan is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Zhihua Yao and completed a PhD at the University of Hong Kong under the supervision of K. L. Dhammajoti.
Sivadatta Sarma was an Indologist who served as a Sanskrit teacher and professor at Maharaja Sanskrit College, Jaipur, with posts attested in 1892 and 1929.
Siyong Liang (1904–1954) was an archaeologist who pursued his studies at Tsinghua University and Harvard University (~1924–1930).
Smita Halder is an Indologist and archaeologist who studied under doctoral supervisor Susmita Basu Majumdar and was a research scholar/fellow at The Asiatic Society (attested 2026).

So Takahashi (b. 1938) is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned an M.A. from the University of Tokyo. He held posts at the University of Tokyo and Meijo University, where he was an associate professor and professor.

Sodo Mori (b. 1934) studied at Komazawa and Tokyo universities under Kogen Mizuno, Hajime Nakamura, and G. P. Malalasekera. A specialist in Buddhist studies and Indology, he held posts at Josai and Aichi Gakuin universities.
Sodo Yokoyama (1907–1980) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Antai-ji (1949–1957) under Kodo Sawaki, as well as under Ekō Hashimoto. He taught Joko Shibata.

Soen Nakagawa (1907–1984) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at the First Higher School, the University of Tokyo, and under Gempo Yamamoto. He taught Robert Baker Aitken, Philip Kapleau, Eido Shimano, Maurine Stuart, and John Daido Loori.

Sofija Aleksandrovna Černikova (1936–1995) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. She studied at the National University of Uzbekistan and the University of Delhi, later teaching and serving as docent (1970) at the National University of Uzbekistan.

Sogaku Harada (1871–1961) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Sendan-Rin School and Komazawa University, training under Dokutan Sōsan and Sotan Oka, among others. He was a professor at Komazawa University (1911–1923).
Sogen Asahina (1891–1979) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who studied at Nihon University. He taught Koun Yamada and Kyozo Yamada, and held a post at Kanagawa University.

Sogen Omori (1904–1994) was a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Nihon University and under Seisetsu Seki, Bokuo Seki, and Jirōkichi Yamada. He was head priest at Koho-in and a professor and president at Hanazono University.

Sogyal Rinpoche (1947–2019) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure who studied at the University of Delhi and the University of Cambridge, and under Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, Dudjom Rinpoche, and Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche. He founded Rigpa in 1975.
Sohini Sengupta is a scholar in Indology who is a PhD student at the University of Chicago (attested 2024–2026).
